hero.title: The Kuruwitu Partnership
hero.label: & Living Classroom
hero.text: A 20-year journey of community-led marine conservation. The story of how Kuruwitu's fishers created Kenya's first Community Conservation Area and built a living laboratory for ocean stewardship.

introduction.text: Kuruwitu is where the model was born and where most of Oceans Alive's demonstration and learning activity still takes place.
introduction.text2: Kuruwitu is a living classroom. Within it we run coral-restoration demonstrations, reef and intertidal learning, fisheries and co-management education, school visits, local and international student programs, internships and engagement with community practitioners. This work is undertaken in close collaboration with the Kuruwitu-CBO, the Kuruwitu BMU, local practitioners, schools and technical partners. Oceans Alive acts as a facilitator and program partner.

theOriginStory.heading: The Origin & Leadership of Kuruwitu
theOriginStory.text: In the early 2000s, Kuruwitu's fishers saw their catch declining year after year. Instead of waiting for outside intervention, they took action themselves.
theOriginStory.text2: Led by local community leaders and fishermen, the
theOriginStory.text3: was formed. In 2003, they established Kenya's first Community Conservation Area (CCA) - a voluntary no-take zone managed entirely by the community.
theOriginStory.text4: This wasn't a project imposed from outside. It was born from local wisdom, driven by local leadership, and sustained by local commitment. The fishers of Kuruwitu decided their future - and created a model that would inspire conservation efforts across Kenya's coast.

livingClassroom.heading: Kuruwitu as a Living Classroom
livingClassroom.text: From local school visits to international student programmes, Kuruwitu hosts hands-on learning experiences in marine conservation and community-led stewardship.

legalContext.heading: Legal & Management Context
legalContext.text: The Kuruwitu closure began as a voluntary community initiative. Over two decades, it evolved into a legally recognized governance model.
legalContext.text3: became Kenya's first legal Co-Management Plan under the Fisheries Management and Development Act (2016). This milestone placed 12,000 hectares of ocean under formal community stewardship.

legalContext.label: The Kuruwitu BMU (community governance)
